brand_model: Sprint Quattro Secure S 6935M + Crome HF Quad CRT-D
electrical_manifestation: connector-port problem / loss of seating
intervention: pocket reopened; lead removed and fully reinserted
evidence_basis: Direct surgical inspection found RV lead not fully seated; correction was reseating.
notes: Two MDR keys describe the same clinical event; count once.

electrical_manifestation: lead could not fully insert
evidence_basis: Returned-product analysis found RV contact spring displaced from ring slot and blocking the connector bore.
notes: No header dimensional anomaly found; whether spring geometry predisposed is unresolved.

brand_model: Cobalt XT HF Quad CRT-D DTPA2Q1
electrical_manifestation: noise + undefined high pacing impedance
evidence_basis: Returned-device analysis traced failure to open RV-tip connection; no weld at interconnect ribbon to setscrew block.
notes: Not a lead-pin contact failure; retain as distinct header-internal mechanism.

electrical_manifestation: failure to disconnect chronic leads
intervention: header broken to remove leads; generator replaced
evidence_basis: Returned-product analysis found blood in atrial and ventricular connector bores bonding lead surfaces to bore.
notes: Manufacturer attributed blood to inadequate cleaning of proximal lead before original insertion; not seal failure.

electrical_manifestation: atrial lead could not be removed
evidence_basis: Returned-product analysis confirmed blood accumulation in atrial connector-port zones causing adhesion.
notes: Setscrew was not causal.

electrical_manifestation: setscrew could not be loosened
evidence_basis: Analysis found calcified blood filling setscrew cavity via a torque-wrench puncture in the septum.
notes: Distinct chronic interface-aging/contamination phenotype.

electrical_manifestation: telemetry loss reported; premature depletion suspected but not confirmed
evidence_basis: Analysis found header bonding anomaly, body fluid at connector bore, feedthrough damage, hermeticity breach, and fluid ingress to internal electronics; battery/current drain normal.
notes: Do not count as lead-terminal/header-contact failure; important adjacent generator-package mechanism.

electrical_manifestation: loose/intermittent connection
evidence_basis: Returned-product analysis confirmed stripped atrial setscrew with septum material preventing full torque-driver insertion.
notes: Anomaly considered procedure-associated.

electrical_manifestation: loose/intermittent connection; high impedance reported
evidence_basis: Returned-product analysis confirmed stripped RV setscrew and septum material preventing full driver insertion.
notes: High impedance itself was not confirmed on analysis.

electrical_manifestation: setscrew could not secure LV lead
evidence_basis: Mechanical analysis found rounded LV setscrew inset with grooves consistent with incorrect wrench insertion.
notes: Procedure-associated, not spontaneous late interface failure.

electrical_manifestation: LV lead could not be inserted/secured
evidence_basis: Analysis found LV setscrew turned down into connector port, physically blocking lead insertion; function restored after backing it out.
notes: Manufacturer classified as user-related.

electrical_manifestation: setscrew could not be tightened
evidence_basis: Returned-product visual analysis found stripped RV setscrew; header bore dimensions normal.
notes: Consistent with procedural damage.

electrical_manifestation: high impedance + high thresholds when lead incompletely seated
intervention: candidate generator not implanted; another generator used
evidence_basis: Chronic lead could not be fully seated in replacement generator port despite repeated attempts; abnormal measurements occurred only in that device.
notes: Needs exact lead model and returned-device analysis before assigning header vs lead-terminal cause.

electrical_manifestation: terminal pin would not pass setscrew block; no electrical failure
intervention: sterile mineral oil enabled full seating
evidence_basis: RV IS-1 terminal appeared larger than atrial terminal; same RV terminal initially failed in both new ICD ports while atrial lead fit both.
notes: More consistent with terminal fit/friction than generator-header defect.

electrical_manifestation: high/undefined pacing impedance on several vectors
intervention: old CRT-P replaced; same lead normal with new device
evidence_basis: Lead tested normally on analyzer; repeated reseating into first generator retained high impedance; new generator produced normal impedance.
notes: Strong device/header localization but no returned-product root cause in available narrative.

brand_model: Sprint Quattro Secure S 6935M with CRT-D
electrical_manifestation: noise + pacing impedance swings; pocket manipulation reproducible
clinical_consequence: therapies deactivated; no patient complication reported
intervention: pocket opened; lead reconnected; generator replaced
evidence_basis: Lead tested normally on analyzer; after reconnection some noise persisted and gentle traction once disengaged lead from header; new generator tested normally.
notes: Highly relevant late interface phenotype; exact setscrew/contact root cause unresolved.

brand_model: Crome VR ICD + Sprint Quattro Secure S 6935M
electrical_manifestation: high RV pacing impedance
evidence_basis: Connection was directly evaluated: lead fully seated and stable during push/pull; generator remained in use.
notes: Two MDR keys describe same event; useful negative control against assuming high impedance = header problem.

electrical_manifestation: non-physiological noise / oversensing
evidence_basis: Returned-electrode analysis found cyclic-fatigue fracture with sharp curves ~25 mm from terminal pin.
notes: Header-adjacent presentation but root cause was lead-body fracture.

electrical_manifestation: oversensed non-physiological noise
intervention: reprogrammed to secondary vector; continued evaluation
evidence_basis: Imaging showed appropriate electrode insertion and possible air entrapment; header insertion was part of differential but not supported.
notes: Two MDR keys describe same event; retain as mimic/signal-only control.

electrical_manifestation: noise / oversensing; Smart Pass disabled
clinical_consequence: no adverse effect reported in available narrative
evidence_basis: Technical Services ultimately reviewed imaging and confirmed electrode was not fully inserted into header.
notes: Two MDR keys likely same event; strong imaging-confirmed seating example.

brand_model: Cobalt XT VR MRI SureScan DVPA2D1
electrical_manifestation: lead dislodged from header block despite full insertion
evidence_basis: Chronic lead tip was visible at end of bore, yet tightening repeatedly failed to retain lead until intermittent engagement.
notes: Suggests setscrew/header mechanical issue; no returned analysis in available narrative.

electrical_manifestation: difficulty engaging setscrew; difficulty disconnecting RV lead
evidence_basis: Multiple setscrew/wrench engagement failures occurred in one generator; new generator accepted all leads normally.
notes: Root cause not confirmed.

brand_model: Cobalt XT DR MRI SureScan DDPA2D4
electrical_manifestation: lead pin would not fully insert; difficulty removing it
intervention: generator replaced; same lead connected easily to new device
evidence_basis: Failure localized to one generator by successful connection to replacement device; setscrew suspected clinically.
notes: No returned-product confirmation in available narrative.

electrical_manifestation: none attributable
evidence_basis: Small amount of dried blood confirmed in ventricular connector bore; device analysis otherwise normal.
notes: Important negative control: contamination can be present without clinically relevant connector malfunction.

electrical_manifestation: original RV noise/pacing inhibition plus later inability to tighten replacement RV lead
evidence_basis: Manufacturer did not confirm original loose/intermittent connection; later found ventricular setscrew missing from socket due counter-clockwise over-rotation during procedure.
notes: Do not attribute original noise to header merely because a separate procedural setscrew problem occurred during revision.

electrical_manifestation: progressive high shock impedance; pacing/sensing normal
intervention: in-clinic pocket manipulation and shock EGM evaluation recommended
evidence_basis: Shock impedance rose over 3–5 months while bipolar pacing/sensing remained normal; Medtronic Technical Services specifically raised header or spring-contact-to-lead-ring mechanism but said pattern was not classic fretting.
notes: High-value late/in-service hypothesis case; lead remained in service and no root cause was confirmed.
